content: 1. Low blood magnesium levels, also known as hypomagnesemia, can occur and may lead to serious complications such as seizures or heart rhythm disturbances. Individuals taking omeprazole for extended periods or those on other medications that lower magnesium levels are at higher risk. If you experience symptoms such as changes in heart rate, dizziness, muscle spasms, or seizures, stop taking omeprazole and contact your healthcare provider immediately. 2. Low blood calcium levels, or hypocalcemia, may also occur. This condition can exacerbate other health issues, particularly in individuals with pre-existing conditions affecting calcium metabolism. 3. Omeprazole may interact with other medications and supplements. Before starting omeprazole, inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are currently using. This is crucial to avoid potential drug interactions. Refer to the interactions section for more details. 4. Omeprazole may affect pregnancy, but it is not definitively known whether it can harm an unborn baby. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your healthcare provider. They will determine whether omeprazole is appropriate for you during pregnancy. 5. Omeprazole should not be taken while breastfeeding, as it can pass into breast milk. Discuss alternative treatments with your healthcare provider if you are nursing. 6. Omeprazole should be taken before meals. It is unclear whether alcohol consumption affects the efficacy of omeprazole. Always consult your healthcare provider regarding dietary or lifestyle considerations while on this medication. 7. Omeprazole can interact with specific medications, such as clopidogrel (Plavix), cilostazol (Pletal), citalopram, methotrexate, digoxin (Lanoxin), warfarin, certain antiretroviral drugs (e.g., rilpivirine, nelfinavir, saquinavir), St. John’s Wort, and rifampin. These interactions may alter the effectiveness of omeprazole or the other medications. Always inform your healthcare provider about all medications you are taking or have recently taken. 8. If you or someone else has taken too much omeprazole, seek immediate medical attention by calling 911 or contacting a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. 9. If you miss a dose of omeprazole, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. 10. Omeprazole is used to treat heartburn and conditions caused by excessive stomach acid, such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), ulcers, erosive esophagitis, and Helicobacter pylori infections. It may also be prescribed for other conditions as determined by your healthcare provider. 11. Omeprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach, which helps alleviate symptoms and promote healing of acid-related conditions. 12. Omeprazole is available in various forms, including capsules, tablets, and packets of powder for delayed-release oral suspension. These are taken by mouth and may be branded as Prilosec, Prilosec OTC, or generic omeprazole. 13. Store omeprazole at room temperature, between 68°F to 77°F (20°C to 25°C). It can tolerate short-term exposure to temperatures between 59°F to 86°F (15°C to 30°C), such as during transportation. Keep it in a cool, dry place. 14. Omeprazole should be swallowed whole. Do not chew, cut, or crush the capsules or tablets. If you have difficulty swallowing, you may open the capsule and sprinkle its contents on one tablespoon of applesauce. Swallow the mixture immediately without chewing. Do not mix it with other foods. 15. Omeprazole is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn. It may take 1 to 4 days for the medication to take full effect. 16. Common side effects of omeprazole include headache, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, gas, and, in children aged 1 to 16 years, infections in the nose or throat and fever. If these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. 17. Serious side effects of omeprazole include kidney problems, such as acute tubulointerstitial nephritis, which can occur at any time during treatment. If you notice decreased urine output or blood in your urine, contact your doctor immediately. 18. Antibiotic-associated diarrhea caused by Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) overgrowth in the gut can occur during omeprazole treatment. Symptoms include watery diarrhea, persistent diarrhea, blood in stool, severe stomach cramps, and fever. Contact your healthcare provider immediately if these symptoms develop. 19. Severe skin reactions, such as Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) and Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN), can occur and may be life-threatening. Symptoms include painful red or purple skin that peels, flat red rashes or blisters on the skin, mouth, nose, or genitals, and red, painful, watery eyes. Stop taking omeprazole and seek emergency medical attention if these symptoms occur. 20. Omeprazole can cause a severe allergic reaction called Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS), which may affect multiple organs, including the liver, kidneys, and heart. Symptoms include skin rash, fever, swollen lymph nodes, shortness of breath, swelling in the legs, dark urine, and yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice). Stop taking omeprazole and seek immediate medical attention if these symptoms occur. 21. Omeprazole may cause or worsen lupus, an autoimmune disorder. Symptoms include new or worsening joint pain and a rash on the arms or cheeks. Inform your healthcare provider if these symptoms develop. 22. Long-term use of omeprazole (3 years or more) may lead to vitamin B12 deficiency, as it reduces the absorption of this vitamin. Symptoms include a sore tongue, weakness, and tingling or numbness in the hands or feet. Contact your healthcare provider if these symptoms occur. 23. Omeprazole can cause low magnesium levels (hypomagnesemia), which may result in seizures, heart rhythm problems, dizziness, or muscle spasms. Individuals taking omeprazole for extended periods or those on other medications that lower magnesium levels are at higher risk. Contact your healthcare provider if you experience these symptoms. 24. Long-term or high-dose use of omeprazole may increase the risk of bone loss and fractures, particularly in older adults. Discuss this risk with your healthcare provider if you are on prolonged treatment. 25. Omeprazole may cause serious allergic reactions, including difficulty breathing, wheezing, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, and skin rash or hives. Stop taking the medication and seek emergency medical attention if these symptoms occur. 26. Omeprazole should not be used by individuals allergic to omeprazole, Prilosec, Prilosec OTC, other proton pump inhibitors, or any ingredients in the specific product. Consult your pharmacist for a complete list of ingredients. 27. Omeprazole should not be taken with certain medications due to potential interactions. Inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are using. 28. Do not take omeprazole unless prescribed by a healthcare provider. Follow the prescribed dosage and do not share the medication with others, even if they have similar symptoms. Keep omeprazole out of reach of children.
